newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS-Dollar vols stay calm with spot off highs.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Dollar vols stay calm with spot off highs.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/pair options edged up Monday as the dollar firmed versus the mark and yen, but trading was subdued ahead of Tuesday's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, dealers and analysts said.
With the dollar holding near 1.7955 marks, below the recent highs, and 116 yen, options traders lack incentive to bid up volatility, said Alan Revercomb, options strategist for I.D.E.A. Inc.
"You've got a dollar that's trending higher that does not scare options traders too much," said Revercomb. "The dollar is progressing higher at a very orderly pace."
Unless the spot spikes higher, rather than plodding upward, volatilities are likely to remain subdued, he said.
The slight gains in volatility reflect the typical readjustment of values after the weekend, following their markdown on Friday to account for time decay, said a U.S. bank trader.

One-month dollar/mark volatility was quoted at 9.85/10.00 percent, up about 0.1 percentage point from Friday, while one-month dollar/yen volatility was at 9.70/10.00 percent, up about 0.2 percentage point.

Risk reversals were little changed from the previous session as well. The one-month 25-delta dollar/mark risk reversal stood at 0.3/0.6 favoring mark puts, and the dollar/yen risk reversal was 0.4/0.6 favoring yen calls.
"Most of the risk reversals in dollar pairs are not really specifying any bias one way or the other," noted Revercomb.

In the quiet atmosphere, dealers are receiving more customer inquiries regarding range binary strategies, Revercomb said. Increased interest in such strategies ultimately tends to have a calming effect on volatilities, he added.
The U.S. bank trader said a $2 billion purchase of one-year dollar calls/French franc puts was a highlight of the options trading day.

Dollar/mark and dollar/French volatility spreads have converged in recent weeks amid renewed faith in European monetary union, the trader said. One-month dollar/French volatility was pegged at 9.70/9.90 percent.
